text:
Marta: quick RFC follow-up — posting a short plan for v4->v5 migration. main problem: a lot of clients still send the old envelope and some use streaming websockets. thinking header-gated compat + a small drop-in shim as a fallback. thoughts?

Kevin: curious about the streaming case — header gating works for HTTP but websockets don't carry the same headers after handshake.

Marta: yeah — for WS we can detect at handshake (subprotocol or query param) and attach a compatibility adapter on the proxy side. not ideal but avoids changing client payloads.

Alim: WRT telemetry, we should emit a per-request compat metric and a migration tag so we can track request quality regressed by mode. also add a feature flag for tenant opt-in.

Marta: agreed. proposal summary: 1) X-RW-Compat header opt-in (clients set X-RW-Compat: v4) 2) proxy-side header-router that rewrites to v5 envelope only for opted-in requests 3) websocket: handshake detection + sidecar adapter 4) fallback shim service for unknown clients with rate-limited passthrough.

Kevin: will the adapter rewrite token auth or any signing? might be risky to touch auth headers.

Marta: keep auth intact. adapter only rewrites body shape and adds a small metadata envelope. nothing touching Authorization.

Leo: how do we surface errors if adapter fails? we should avoid 500s for user requests. return 4xx with clear migration code and link to migration doc. e.g., 422 MIGRATE_BODY_SHIM_REQUIRED.

Alim: +1. also prefer gradual rollout by tenant — flag in account config. then we can back out per-tenant.

Marta: rollout plan draft: stage 0: feature flag + telemetry (no rewrites). stage 1: opt-in header enabled for a subset of internal tenants. stage 2: enable sidecar adapter for WS for same tenants. stage 3: public opt-in. stage 4: enable passive shim (logs-only) and monitor for errors. stage 5: consider enforcement after 90d notice.

Kevin: we need a canary test harness that runs real prompts through both v4 and translated-to-v5 path and checks tokenization/rolling context equivalence. can we shell out to the eval infra?

Alim: yep I can wire a small CI job to run a micro-eval set every hour. will emit a perf delta + quality delta metric.

Marta: config snippet for header gate (example):

```yaml
compat:
  header: X-RW-Compat
  modes: [v4, v5]
  default: v5
```

Marta: WS handshake detection example: client uses subprotocol `rw-compat-v4` or query `?compat=v4`. proxy stores compat tag in request meta.

Kevin: do we need a dedicated shim binary or can we reuse adapter code in the proxy? reusing reduces deployment surface but might bloat proxy.

Marta: prefer small sidecar shim service for easier rollback. it will be a single API: POST /translate { envelope: v4 } -> { envelope: v5 } and idempotent. keep it minimal.

Leo: for rate-limited passthrough, add a circuit-breaker so if the shim is overloaded we 1) log and 2) return 422 with migration hint, not degrade into silent failures.

sre-bot: deploy scheduled: compat-sidecar-preview -> infra/compat/v1 at 2024-07-12T03:00Z (staged canary).

Alim: I'll add compat metrics: compat.opt_in.count, compat.translation.latency_ms, compat.translation.errors. add tags: tenant_id, route, mode.

Marta: docs todo: migration guide snippet, header examples, websocket handshake samples, rollback steps, telemetry dashboards. I'll draft the guide and ping @kevin for the streaming bits.

Kevin: ok, I'll prototype the handshake detector and websocket sidecar. estimate 2w + tests.

Marta: thanks. next sync: quick async check-in in #eng-platform next Tues. if anyone objects to the plan raise now. :raised_hands:

Leo: +1 from infra ops. let's keep the error codes consistent with existing migration errors.

Alim: noted — I'll add schema to the telemetry and the alert thresholds.

Marta: perfect — closing for now. will open a tiny RFC PR with the rollout phases and links to the shim repo.
